title: What staff training do the RACGP Standards require for general practice accreditation?
description: Staff training in the RACGP Standards for general practices: 5th edition CPR, role and infection control indicators, and what the new 6th edition adds.
shortAnswer: As at November 2026, general practices accredited under the National General Practice Accreditation Scheme are assessed against the Royal Australian College of General Practitioners (RACGP) Standards for general practices (5th edition). Non-clinical staff need role-appropriate training and CPR at least once every three years (C8.1). Clinicians need registration, CPD and CPR (GP3.1). A named clinician must educate the team on infection control (GP4.1). A 6th edition is released, with transition timing not yet announced.
keyTakeaways: Accreditation under the National General Practice Accreditation (NGPA) Scheme still uses the 5th edition. The Australian Commission on Safety and Quality in Health Care (ACSQHC) will announce when assessments move to the 6th edition.
Indicator C8.1 B requires non-clinical staff to complete CPR training at least once every three years, and the RACGP states that CPR training completed solely online does not meet the requirement.
Indicator GP3.1 A requires clinical team members to hold current registration, participate in CPD, and train in CPR as their professional organization recommends or at least every three years.
Indicator GP4.1 C requires a clinical team member with primary responsibility for educating the practice team about infection prevention and control.
The 6th edition's criterion F4 adds ongoing role-appropriate training, Medicare billing education, and training in recognizing and responding to family, domestic and sexual violence.
regulator: Royal Australian College of General Practitioners (RACGP), as standards author; Australian Commission on Safety and Quality in Health Care (ACSQHC), as operator of the National General Practice Accreditation Scheme
appliesTo: General practices and health services seeking accreditation against the RACGP Standards for general practices
Practice owners and practice managers responsible for training records
Non-clinical staff such as reception and administration teams
GPs, registrars, practice nurses and other clinical team members

sections.heading: Which edition of the RACGP Standards applies to accreditation in November 2026?

blocks.text: The 5th edition. The ACSQHC's [NGPA Scheme page](https://www.safetyandquality.gov.au/accreditation/national-general-practice-accreditation-ngpa-scheme) says the scheme "currently uses the 5th edition", while encouraging practices to begin using the guidance in the newly released 6th edition as they review their systems and engage their workforce.

The RACGP's page on [what practices need to know about the sixth edition](https://www.racgp.org.au/running-a-practice/practice-standards/standards-6th-edition/standards-6th-edition-hub/what-practices-need-to-know) says information about transition timing and accreditation requirements "will be communicated by the Australian Commission on Safety and Quality in Health Care", and that all practices undergoing accreditation will need to meet the 6th edition after the transition period. Training programs built now should therefore satisfy the 5th edition indicators and be ready to map to the 6th edition criteria.

blocks.title: In transition
blocks.text: As at November 2026 the 6th edition is published and has ISQua accreditation, but no date for assessment against it had been set on the ACSQHC or RACGP pages reviewed. The 5th edition criterion pages cited here were last revised on 24 February 2023. Confirm the current position with your accrediting agency before an assessment.

sections.heading: How does accreditation against the Standards work?

blocks.text: A practice is assessed by an accrediting agency approved under the NGPA Scheme, which the RACGP says commenced on 1 January 2017. According to the RACGP's [accreditation section of the 5th edition](https://www.racgp.org.au/running-a-practice/practice-standards/standards-5th-edition/standards-for-general-practices-5th-ed/introduction-to-the-standards-for-general-practice/accreditation), the cycle is three years, surveyor teams have at least two surveyors (one an appropriately qualified GP), and an eligible practice "must still meet all mandatory indicators in the Standards to be accredited".

Eligibility depends on providing comprehensive, continuous care that is predominantly general practice: more than 50% of the GPs' collective clinical time and more than 50% of Medicare services claimed or claimable. The RACGP describes accreditation itself as a voluntary scheme. Surveyors look for records, so the training indicators below are only met if the practice can produce evidence.

sections.heading: What training must non-clinical staff complete under the 5th edition?

blocks.text: Non-clinical staff must complete training appropriate to their role and patient population, and CPR training at least once every three years. These are the two indicators of [Criterion C8.1](https://www.racgp.org.au/running-a-practice/practice-standards/standards-5th-edition/standards-for-general-practices-5th-ed/core-standards/core-standard-8/criterion-c8-1-education-and-training-of-non-clini), Education and training of non-clinical staff.

items: **C8.1 A:** "Our non-clinical staff complete training appropriate to their role and our patient population." The practice must provide evidence that non-clinical staff have completed all relevant training.
**C8.1 B:** "Our non-clinical staff complete cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training at least once every three years." The practice must provide evidence of completion within that interval.

blocks.text: The RACGP's guidance on C8.1 lists topics such as practice procedures, technology, first aid, medical terminology, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander cultural awareness, communicating with patients who have communication needs, and safe operation of equipment. It also suggests demonstrating that non-clinical staff have completed infection prevention and control training appropriate to their role and know who in the practice is responsible for infection control. Reception staff recognizing a medical emergency at the front desk is named as a suitable in-house topic.

The CPR rules are specific. Training must comply with Australian Resuscitation Council guidelines and include operating an automated external defibrillator. It can be delivered by an accredited provider or by a clinician holding a current CPR instructor's certificate. Trainees must physically demonstrate their skills at the end, and "CPR training that is completed solely online does not meet this requirement".

sections.heading: What do the Standards require of the clinical team's training?

blocks.text: Clinical team members must hold current registration where applicable, participate in CPD, train in CPR, and be trained on the practice equipment they use. These requirements sit in [Criterion GP3.1](https://www.racgp.org.au/running-a-practice/practice-standards/standards-5th-edition/standards-for-general-practices-5th-ed/general-practice-standards/gp-standard-3/criterion-gp3-1-qualifications-education-and-train), Qualifications, education and training of healthcare practitioners.

items: **GP3.1 A:** clinicians have current national registration where applicable, accreditation or certification with their professional association, active CPD in line with legal and professional requirements, and CPR training "in accordance with the recommendations of their professional organisation, or at least every three years".
**GP3.1 B:** GPs are vocationally registered, on a pathway to Fellowship, supervised registrars, or working under an approved workforce program.
**GP3.1 C:** the clinical team is trained to use the practice equipment needed to perform their role safely and effectively.

blocks.text: The criterion makes CPD a practice-level evidence point, not only a matter between a practitioner and their Board. A practice should hold proof of each clinician's registration and CPD compliance, which links to the Board requirements in [what CPD Ahpra requires](/regulations/ahpra-cpd-registration-standards) and to the separate question of granting clinicians a defined scope, covered in [credentialing and scope of clinical practice](/regulations/credentialing-and-scope-of-clinical-practice-australia).

sections.heading: What infection control training does Criterion GP4.1 expect?

blocks.text: The practice must name a clinical team member responsible for educating the whole team about infection prevention and control, and every team member must manage cross-infection risks. [Criterion GP4.1](https://www.racgp.org.au/running-a-practice/practice-standards/standards-5th-edition/standards-for-general-practices-5th-ed/general-practice-standards/gp-standard-4/criterion-gp4-1-infection-prevention-and-control-i) sets six indicators, three of which drive training content.

items: **GP4.1 A:** at least one clinical team member has primary responsibility for coordinating infection control, sterile equipment, reprocessing procedures, sterile stock rotation and waste management.
**GP4.1 C:** a clinical team member has primary responsibility for educating the practice team about infection prevention and control.

**GP4.1 D:** all team members manage cross-infection risks through hand hygiene, PPE, triage of patients with potential communicable diseases, safe storage and disposal of clinical waste including sharps, and safe management of blood and body fluid spills.

blocks.text: Indicator GP4.1 D applies to everyone, including reception staff who triage patients with respiratory symptoms. A practice that trains only nurses on PPE and spills leaves a gap a surveyor can find by asking a receptionist what happens when a patient arrives with a suspected infectious illness.

sections.heading: How do the training indicators map to roles, frequency and evidence?

blocks.text: Each indicator can be turned into a row in a practice [training matrix](/glossary/training-matrix) with an owner, an interval and the record a surveyor will ask for. This illustrative table, prepared for this page, lines up the 5th edition indicators, with the 6th edition criterion that will absorb each one. It is not an RACGP template.

blocks.text: Because the Standards set only the CPR interval, the other refresher periods are the practice's decision and should be written down with a reason. The guide to [setting mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles) gives a method, and [how to build a training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix) covers the structure.

sections.heading: What does the 6th edition change for staff training?

blocks.text: The 6th edition gathers induction, training and performance support into criterion F4 and widens its scope. The RACGP's article on [induction, training and supporting performance](https://www.racgp.org.au/running-a-practice/practice-standards/standards-6th-edition/standards-6th-edition-hub/induction-training-and-supporting-performance) lists structured induction for all team members, ongoing role-appropriate training for employed team members, performance discussions, and CPR training "for all staff at least every three years".

items: **Ongoing training:** employed team members receive role-appropriate training when they start and continuing training as systems, technologies and practice needs change.
**Medicare billing:** employed team members know how to access Medicare billing education resources.

**Abuse and violence:** practices confirm that employed team members have completed role-appropriate training in recognizing and responding to family, domestic and sexual violence, and obtain reasonable assurance that independent doctors have done the same.

**Structure:** the edition has four standards (Foundations, Clinical governance, Patient participation, and Continuous quality improvement) and replaces flagged and unflagged indicators with criteria that are mandatory unless labelled aspirational.
**Artificial intelligence:** criterion F11 applies only to practices that use AI tools.

blocks.text: The family violence requirement overlaps with state child protection duties for some staff; those are covered in [mandatory reporting training in Australia](/regulations/mandatory-reporting-training-australia). Further context on training across care settings is on the [healthcare and life sciences](/industries/healthcare-life-sciences) page.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: A practice preparing for accreditation during an edition change needs every training record tied to the indicator it satisfies and to its successor criterion. Knowledge Foundry holds the 5th and 6th edition requirements as linked items, so a CPR certificate or an infection control session is recorded once and reported against whichever edition the surveyor assesses. When the ACSQHC sets the transition date, the gaps, such as family violence training for independent doctors, are already identified by role.

faqs.q: Do reception staff in a general practice need CPR training?
faqs.a: Yes, for an accredited practice. Indicator C8.1 B of the 5th edition requires non-clinical staff to complete CPR training at least once every three years, and the 6th edition keeps CPR training for all staff at least every three years. The training must include a physical skills demonstration and use of an automated external defibrillator.

faqs.q: Does online CPR training count for RACGP accreditation?
faqs.a: Not on its own. The RACGP states that the Australian Resuscitation Council requires trainees to physically demonstrate their skills at the end of the course, and that CPR training completed solely online does not meet the requirement. A blended course with an in-person assessment can meet it.

faqs.q: Can a practice choose to be accredited against the 6th edition now?
faqs.a: As at November 2026 the ACSQHC says accreditation under the NGPA Scheme currently uses the 5th edition, and the RACGP says the ACSQHC will communicate transition timing. Practices are encouraged to use the 6th edition guidance now while being assessed against the 5th.

faqs.q: Who can deliver CPR training in a general practice?
faqs.a: An accredited training provider, or a member of the clinical team who holds a current CPR instructor's certificate that complies with Australian Resuscitation Council guidelines on instructor competencies. The training itself must follow Australian Resuscitation Council guidelines.

faqs.q: Do the Standards require infection control training for every staff member?
faqs.a: Indicator GP4.1 D requires all members of the practice team to manage cross-infection risks through hand hygiene, PPE, triage, waste and sharps handling, and spill management, and GP4.1 C requires a clinician responsible for educating the team. The guidance for C8.1 also suggests evidencing role-appropriate infection control training for non-clinical staff.
